citations.text: Inspected the attached scan pixels. The actual headword is 一, with reading yī and phonological labels “影组、质部; 影组、质韵、於悉切.” The entry calls it a 指事字, says the ancient graphs 一 through 四 use one to four horizontal strokes as primitive counting symbols, and identifies its basic meaning as the smallest positive integer. It cites 玉篇 and 尚書《洪範》 for “one as the beginning of number” and ordinal use. It says that from the Spring and Autumn/Warring States period 一 could be written with added strokes/components as elaborated forms, analogous to forms of 二 and 三, and that these spellings later fell out of use. This paraphrase relies on the scan-verified claims, not an emendation of its printed forms.

citations.text: Directly checked the illustrated entry and the key against the scan: the sequence is labeled Shang, Western Zhou, Spring and Autumn, Warring States, Shuowen small seal, Han clerical, Shuowen ancient form, and Han/other referenced forms. The entry's bibliography points to 甲文編, 金文編, 類編, 郭店, 說文 and 篆隸表. These printed labels establish what this book presents, but the scan is not itself the underlying inscription source and does not independently validate each cited glyph reading.

citations.field: PDF p. 13, printed forms in sentence beginning 春秋战国以后; scan SHA-256 ca587c8650396b510459c0da1f819d61c79392b822061989f317be87bc9fb70a
citations.text: Scan inspection confirms the text literally prints duplicated-looking forms in the comparison: 一可写作“弌”或 a second form visually resembling 弌; 二可写作“弍” or a second visually matching form; 三可写作“弎” or a form appearing as “弍”. Because these printed rare forms do not all resolve cleanly to distinct Unicode identities from the scan, the wording above summarizes only the unambiguous claim of elaborated spellings. No guessed correction has been substituted.
